chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Ismail, from Hanaan, who said:

I was sitting in the presence of Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him). Mu'ammarr the oil merchant said to him, 'We buy the oil in its skins (zigaq), and a deficiency is calculated for us in it due to the place of the skin.' He (peace be upon him) said, 'If it increases and decreases, there is no problem; but if it increases and does not decrease, do not go near it.'

key_terms.زِقَاقِهِ: Its skins (plural of ziq, a leather container for oil)
key_terms.فَلَا بَأْسَ: There is no problem (it is permissible)
key_terms.فَلَا تَقْرَبْهُ: Do not go near it (avoid it)

ai.seo_question: What is the Islamic ruling on buying oil in skins where the container's volume affects the measurement?
ai.summary: In this narration from al-Kafi, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) distinguishes between permissible variable deductions for the weight of the container (zigaq) and impermissible fixed deductions that consistently favor the seller, highlighting the Shia emphasis on precise equity in commercial transactions. This ruling underscores the principle of 'gharar' (uncertainty/deception) in trade, where a static deduction that does not reflect actual container weight is considered a subtle form of exploitation. The hadith serves as a practical guideline for ensuring fairness in daily market interactions, aligning with the broader Islamic legal tradition of preventing hidden losses in sales.

en.hubeali: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Muhammad Bin Ismail, from Hanaan who said,

‘I was seated in the presence of Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>, so Moamar the oil merchant said to him<sup>asws</sup>, ‘We buy the oil in its alley way, so he measures it out for us with a deficiency in it due to the placing of the alleyway’. So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘If it was (sometimes) excess and deficient, so there is no problem; and if it was excess and not (never) deficient, so do not go near it’.
en.sarwar: 4. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Muhammad ibn ‘Isma’il from Hanan who has said the following:

“Once I was sitting in the presence of abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, when Mu’ammar al-Zayyat said, ‘We buy oil in Ziqaq (a certain container), they compensate it for deficit because of Ziqaq. He (the Imam) said, ‘If it comes extra as well as in deficit, it is not harmful but if it comes extra and no deficit, then you must not go close to it.’”
